description: Six planted bugs. Each entry is filed as a GitHub issue with the same number so autofix-agent can be pointed at it.

issues.title: GET /items?limit=N returns N+1 items
issues.body:
## Steps to reproduce

1. Start the API.
2. `curl 'http://localhost:3000/items?limit=2'`

## Expected

The `items` array has at most 2 entries.

## Actual

The `items` array has 3 entries. `limit=1` returns 2, `limit=4` returns 5. The `limit` field in the response body is correct, only the slice is wrong.

This breaks every client that pages with `offset += limit`: the last item of each page is repeated as the first item of the next page.

issues.title: Discount is subtracted as a dollar amount instead of a percentage
issues.body:
`GET /items/2/price?discount=10` should apply a 10 % discount to the Standing Desk (399.00) and return `359.10`.

It returns `389` instead: the endpoint subtracts 10 dollars, not 10 percent.

The README and the JSDoc on `applyDiscount` both say the second argument is a percentage between 0 and 100. `discount=0` and the range check still behave correctly.

issues.title: PUT /items/:id returns the updated item but the change is not persisted
issues.body:
```
curl -X PUT localhost:3000/items/3 -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"quantity": 5}'
# -> 200 {"id":3,"name":"Notebook",...,"quantity":5}
curl localhost:3000/items/3
# -> 200 {"id":3,"name":"Notebook",...,"quantity":120}
```

The PUT response looks right, but a following GET (and the list endpoint) still show the old values. Renaming an item has the same problem: the new slug shows up in the PUT response only.

Expected: after a successful PUT, GET /items/:id returns the updated fields.

issues.title: Search is case-sensitive although it is documented as case-insensitive
issues.body:
`GET /items?q=desk` returns no items. `GET /items?q=Desk` returns "Desk Lamp" and "Standing Desk".

The `ItemStore.search` docstring and the README both promise a case-insensitive substring match, and the mobile client lower-cases every query before sending it, so search is effectively broken for it.

Expected: `q=desk`, `q=DESK` and `q=Desk` all return the same two items.

issues.title: DELETE /items/:id with an unknown id returns 204 and deletes a different item
issues.body:
## Steps to reproduce

1. `curl -X DELETE localhost:3000/items/999` -> `204 No Content`
2. `curl localhost:3000/items` -> only 4 items; "USB-C Cable" (id 5) is gone.

## Expected

`404 {"error":"item not found"}` and no change to the store.

## Notes

Deleting an existing id works. It looks like the store removes *something* even when the id is not found. This is data loss, please prioritise.

issues.title: slugify leaves a trailing hyphen when the name ends with punctuation
issues.body:
Creating an item named `Hello World!` gives the slug `hello-world-`. `Mr. Coffee` gives `mr-coffee` (fine) but `  Spaced  ` gives `-spaced-`.

Expected: no leading or trailing hyphens, so `Hello World!` -> `hello-world` and `  Spaced  ` -> `spaced`. Interior hyphens should stay as they are (`USB-C Cable` -> `usb-c-cable` must keep working).
